<h2 id="toc-1">Snippet information retrieval officially launched in February</h2>
<p>last year<a class="rank-math-link" href="./seo-newsletter-issue-18.html#toc-1">Search OnActivity</a>The mentioned progress of Google's ranking algorithm was originally expected to be launched at the end of 2020, but it did not materialize.<strong>Finally, in February 2021, the official account confirmed that this update has been officially launched. It started with English searches in the United States and gradually expanded to every language in the world. After the complete launch, it will affect about 7% of search terms.</strong></p>

<h2 id="toc-2">Google provides more information about domains on the SERP</h2>
<p>There will now be a mark in the upper right corner of the search results, allowing users to click to see more information about the "website". The source of this information is Wikipedia, so for larger websites, the description on Wikipedia will be more important, and attention should be paid to reputation management in this area.</p>
<p>This feature is currently available in English search results in the United States and appears on both computers and mobile devices.</p>

<h2 id="toc-3">Discover reports in GSC will be included in Chrome data</h2>
<p>When the mobile version of Chrome opens a new tab, it will actively recommend web pages (articles) below. This part of the traffic will also be recorded in the Discover report in Search Console in the future. However, currently<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://twitter.com/JohnMu/status/1356705552240435204">no way</a>Distinguish Discover traffic from different sources (Chrome or Google App).</p>

<h2 id="toc-4">Rumor: GSC adds more filters (web experience, registration content...etc.)</h2>
<p>When JR Oakes dug into the code of Google Search Console, he saw signs that future filters might add "Page Experience", "Subscribed Content", "Cross-language results", and some new conditions that are not currently available.</p>
<blockquote class="embed embed--twitter"><p>Twitter/X Post</p><a href="https://twitter.com/jroakes/status/1359480446153879553" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original post on Twitter/X</a></blockquote>
<p><strong>This is just a possible update dug up through reverse engineering. It does not mean that it will definitely be realized. No one knows the exact definition of each condition, so everyone can just treat it as a rumor.</strong> </p>
<p>Google has said in the past, “<em><a class="rank-math-link" href="https://www.seroundtable.com/google-page-experience-indicator-no-30749.html">All three CWVs achieve excellent web pages, and there will be an icon indicating "may" in the search results.</a></em>”, the Page Experience filtering in the message seems to have something to do with this news.</p>

<h2 id="toc-6">Google will ban e-commerce websites with different checkout amounts</h2>
<p>Google did it<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/10307781">An announcement</a>, starting from 4/6, if during the checkout process, the e-commerce website will receive a warning if the checkout amount is higher than the price announced in the advertisement or webpage, and the Merchant Center account may be suspended as a result.</p>
<p>There was such an article in the Wall Street Post last year
Report by<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://www.wsj.com/articles/who-is-the-mystery-shopper-leaving-behind-all-those-online-shopping-carts-11593617464"></a>, many e-commerce websites found that a person named John Smith would add items to the shopping cart but not check out, and would repeat this behavior, causing trouble in analysis. Finally, it was discovered that Google automatically added the items to the shopping cart in order to ensure that the final checkout amount matched the price on the page.</p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>
<div class="wp-block-group"><div class="wp-block-group__inner-container">
<h2 id="toc-7">Tip: See if Google has rendering issues in full</h2>
<p>This is a little trick I learned recently. You can use URL Inspection in GSC to see the rendered HTML of the web page, as well as screenshots.<strong>However, the screenshot can only slide to a certain extent and the rendering of the entire page cannot be seen.</strong>, and through the following method, you can see what the entire web page looks like in the eyes of Google!</p>
<ol><li>Go to the page to be tested</li><li>Open Chrome DevTools &gt; Elements</li><li>Right click &lt;html&gt; &gt; Edit as HTML</li><li>Select all and delete</li><li>Copy the HTML given by URL Inspection</li><li>Paste it back into Chrome DevTools to see what the web page looks like as seen by Googlebot</li></ol>
<p>Because GSC gives the rendered HTML, it is already known that those resources failed to load, and this step further uses Chrome to draw the rendered HTML.</p>
<p>Tip source:<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://www.contentkingapp.com/academy/url-inspection-tool/#view-tested-page:~:text=To%20diagnose%20rendering%20issues%3A">Oliver Mason</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>

<h2 id="toc-9">Case: Internal links increase web page traffic by 7%</h2>
<p>The website in this case is a real estate company with about 8,000 "local" pages. These pages are not orphan pages. They have pages from breadcrumbs or other places, but there is no more systematic link between them.</p>
<p>They decided to test "<em>Add a Nearby Locations section to the place page and put an internal link to the place page in the nearby area.</em>". As a result, the natural traffic of the tested group increased by 7% compared with the control group.</p>
<div class="wp-block-image"><figure class="aligncenter size-large is-resized"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 26 – 2021.02.01~2021.02.15" class="wp-image-2569" decoding="async" height="236" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2021/02/%E5%85%A7%E9%83%A8%E9%80%A3%E7%B5%90-SEO-%E6%A1%88%E4%BE%8B-1.png" width="234"/><figcaption>Internal link block</figcaption></figure></div>

<h2 id="toc-10">Official Video: 12 Tips and Tips for Image SEO</h2>
<p>In this video, John talks about where images will appear on Google searches (images, general results, Discover) and 12 key points for optimizing images, including the following:</p>
<ol><li>provides context about the image (provide context)</li><li>The image position should be placed near relevant content (optimize placement)</li><li>Important text should not be placed in the image (text on the page, not in image)</li><li>Use image ALT tag (use alt-attribute)</li><li>use high-quality images</li><li>Make high-quality sites</li><li>ensures that images are displayed well on mobile phones and computers (works on mobile and desktop)</li><li>Use good image URLs/file names (good, stable, descriptive URLs)</li><li>provide relevant structured data</li><li>consider large image previews</li><li>use markup for image licensing opportunities</li><li>Consider image loading speed (consider speed)</li></ol>
<figure class="embed embed--youtube"><div class="embed__frame"><iframe allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen="" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/SfC27XgelgE" title="YouTube video player"></iframe></div><figcaption><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SfC27XgelgE" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original video on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Although this video is for beginners, it talks about a very important point -<strong>Getting images indexed is actually not a goal that webmasters should be too focused on in many cases.</strong>, you can ask yourself a few questions first, "<em>Do users find your content through visual means?</em>」、「<em>What kind of preview image will make your content more attractive?</em>」、「<em>Are the pictures related to the web content?</em>」。</p>
